# Best power station and solar combos for an RV

The right pick depends on whether you want weekend trips or off-grid living, and whether you need to run a roof AC. Most RVs have a 30A system, so a unit with a 30A RV outlet and high solar input is worth the extra money.

## My picks

**1. Best all-round value: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 200W solar panel kit**
- 2,073.6Wh, 2,600W output, listed at $1,199, or $1,139.05 with code **AFF5OFF** (code tested 2026-10-25).
- This is enough for a fridge, lights, a laptop and Starlink for a day or more.
- [Buy the Elite 200 V2 + 200W kit](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2-200w-solar-kit)
- Source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/)

**2. Best for boondocking with heavy loads: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous and 8,000W surge, expandable past 12kWh. It recharges 0-80% in about 50 minutes from a wall outlet.
- It can run a 13,500 BTU roof AC (about 1,500W running) for roughly 2.3 hours, and it's the most expensive option.
- It's heavy enough to need two people to lift. Buy panels separately.
- Source: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/). That article is written for Ontario, so ignore its Canadian electrical rules, and I didn't get a direct buy link for this one.

**3. Best budget with more solar headroom: BLUETTI AC200L (2,048Wh, 2,400W)**
- It has a built-in 30A RV port and accepts up to 1,200W of solar, so you can add panels later. It weighs about 62 lb.
- $899, or $854.05 with code **AFF5OFF**.
- [Buy the AC200L](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l)
- Sources: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/), [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/), [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

**4. Best lighter, cheaper kit: ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro + 400W solar kit**
- 1,451Wh, 2,400W, with a bigger 400W panel. It's $963, or $866.70 with code **ALLPOWERS26**.
- [Buy the S2000 Pro + SP037 kit](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-s2000-pro-sp037-solar-kit)
- Source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/)

## Things to know
- **A 200W panel recharges slowly.** For regular off-grid use, plan on 400W or more of panels. A 300-400W array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- **Check the unit's solar input limit.** Jackery's 1000 v2 and 2000 v2 cap at 400W, so extra panels won't help ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).
- **Running a roof AC needs a large unit.** An AC spikes above 3,000W at startup, so you need roughly 3,000W+ surge capacity. That points to the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 or the Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro, not the 2,000Wh class.
- **Dealectric's links are affiliate links.** The prices and codes come from that site's own testing on Oct 25-26, so confirm the final price at checkout.

If you tell me what you want to run (roof AC, fridge, Starlink, CPAP) and how many nights off-grid, I can narrow this to one pick.
